_doc: Vocabulary for the geo classifier. Lives in config, not code, because this is the
part that will churn: every week of real ad copy adds a place name nobody predicted.
'DC' throughout this build means the DC MARKET as scoped for this client, not the
District boundary. Movement's monitored gym is in Arlington and Sportrock's is in
Alexandria; an ad pushing either of those is locally relevant to Kyle and is scored
dc_*. A place inside the commuter shed but outside the monitored set (Rockville,
Silver Spring) is 'regional'. Baltimore is not this market.
Matching is case-insensitive, on word boundaries, against the ad's text fields and
landing URLs. First tier that hits wins, and the matched string is stored as evidence.
Landing URL paths that are a location page for one of that brand's gyms inside
the DC-market catchment (the same ~30-minute gate the competitive set was built on).
Keyed by competitor domain, matched as a substring of host+path+query.
DELIBERATE ASYMMETRY: a landing page to Movement Rockville scores dc_landing, but
the word 'Rockville' in body copy scores only 'regional'. Pointing paid traffic at
a specific local asset is a stronger statement of local intent than naming a place
in a sentence, and the tiers are ordered by signal strength, not by geography.
Baltimore-market pages (Timonium, Hampden, Columbia MD) are deliberately absent.

dc_landing_query_hints._doc: Some brands carry the location in a query string or UTM rather than the path. Substring match on the whole lowercased URL. Kept separate so the evidence string says which mechanism fired.

dc_explicit._doc: Place names inside the monitored DC market. A hit here is the second strongest signal after a landing page.
_scope_note: The District plus the inner Arlington/Alexandria ring only. Two of the five
monitored gyms sit in that ring (Movement Crystal City, Sportrock Alexandria),
so it is DC-market by the same logic the competitive set used.
Springfield, Annandale, Sterling and Lorton are outer commuter shed and live in
'regional'. Getting this line wrong inflates the number Kyle reads.

ambiguous._doc: Terms that are DC-market place names AND ordinary words or other-market places. Each carries its OWN disambiguator list; nothing else qualifies it. 'Columbia' alone is Columbia MD, Columbia SC, and Columbia University.

regional._doc: The commuter shed and the umbrella terms. Real, but weaker than a named DC-market place.

_doc: Terms that fire on ordinary prose unless disambiguated. The two-letter state
abbreviations are the worst: 'MD' is a doctor and 'VA' is the start of 'va va
voom'. These are listed ONLY here, never in 'terms' above, or the unconditional
pass matches them first and the qualifier logic never runs.
'Rio' is Sportrock's Gaithersburg gym and also a city in Brazil.
Markets these brands operate in that are NOT this one. A hit here is informative in
its own right: it says the national page is running local creative for somewhere
else, which is the context for a DC-referencing count being low.
Baltimore is deliberately here, not in 'regional'. Movement runs Timonium and
Hampden; they are a different metro and a different competitive question.
Landing-page path patterns applied to EVERY competitor domain, not just the ones
hand-listed above. Real ads in public.signals proved the need: Casper drives to
stores.casper.com/dc/washington/ and VEG to veg.com/locations/dc, both from national
pages whose copy says nothing geographic at all. The per-brand list only catches
paths somebody already thought to write down; if Onelife launches
/gyms/columbia-heights next month, only this list catches it.
Anchored with a leading slash and a trailing boundary so '/dc' does not match
'/dc-comics' and '/washington' does not match '/washingtonville'.
